paper.title: Incentive-Aware Recommender Systems in Two-Sided Markets

settings.name_in_paper: Recommendation under known (homogeneous) opportunity costs with incentive constraints
unmapped: Myopic agents follow a recommendation only if E[X_{I_t}|I_t, E_t] >= c_* (incentive constraint); designer controls information disclosure E_t
Known opportunity cost c_* and known mean mu_1 of arm 1 with mu_1 > c_* (learner_knows mu_star is an approximation: the learner knows mu_1, not necessarily the optimal mean)
Regret defined via loss l(I_t,y_t)=max_i E[X_i - X_{I_t} y_t] depending on agents' actions y_t
Tuning theta_tau depends on min_i P(mu_i - c_* >= tau), a prior-type quantity
settings.definition_quote: Assume that arm $i=1$'s expected reward is known and greater than the cost, $\mu_1>c_*$. ... $R_T = \sum_{t=1}^Tl(I_t,y_t) - \min_{i\in\AA}\sum_{t=1}^Tl(i,y_t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Recommendation under private (unknown, heterogeneous) opportunity costs
unmapped: Rewards stochastic i.i.d. in [0,1] but agents' follow/ignore actions y_t form an arbitrary sequence; bounds hold for any action sequence {y_t}
Regret defined via loss l(I_t,y_t)=max_i E[X_i - X_{I_t} y_t]
settings.definition_quote: Each agent's opportunity cost can be private, heterogenous, and unknown to the designer. ... for any arm set $\AA$ and action sequence $\{y_t\}_{t=1}^T\in\YY^T$

settings.name_in_paper: Recommendation under private opportunity costs, anytime (unknown T)
unmapped: Agents' actions y_t arbitrary sequence; regret via loss l(I_t,y_t)
settings.definition_quote: if MARP in Algorithm 2 is equipped with a time-varying parameter $\eta=\sqrt{8(\ln m)/t}$, then it yields a near-optimal regret bound for any unknown $T$.

algorithms.name: MARP with time-varying eta_t = sqrt(8 ln m / t)

symbols.L_rounds: L^* = L_1+...+L_m, total number of rounds in Step 2 (sampling) of ARP

tuning: k >= max{9/(2 lambda^2) ln(20m/lambda), theta_tau^2 ln(T theta_tau)}

source.label: lem:regretofknowncost
source.quote: Suppose the assumption in Eq.~\eqref{eqn:positiveplat} holds, and the parameters $\lambda,\theta_\tau, k$ are chosen by Eqs.~ ... Let $\gamma_t=1$ in Eq.~\eqref{eqn:egofht}. Then the ARP procedure in Algorithm \ref{alg:adaptivesampling} achieves ex-post regret, $R_T \leq L^*+O\left(\sqrt{mT\ln(mT)}\right)$, where $L^* \equiv L_1+\cdots+L_m$ is the total number of rounds in Step 2 of ARP

results.notes: O(.) applies only to the sqrt term; L^* is additive and itself random/depends on k. Probability type not stated (called ex-post regret); 'expectation' chosen arbitrarily—proof uses elimination bound holding on a good event. m = K.

source.label: thm:regretexpweight
source.quote: If the parameters $\eta=\sqrt{(8\ln m)/T}$ and $\gamma_t\equiv 1$ in Eq.~\eqref{eqn:egofht}, then for any arm set $\AA$ and action sequence $\{y_t\}_{t=1}^T\in\YY^T$, the MARP procedure in Algorithm \ref{alg:MARP} satisfies, with probability at least $1-\delta$ for any $\delta\in(0,1)$, $R_T\leq \sqrt{\frac{T}{2}\ln m} +  \sqrt{\frac{T}{2}\ln\frac{1}{\delta}}$

results.notes: Proof assumes importance-weighted loss estimates in [0,1] (questionable for bandit feedback), but recorded as stated.

conditions: minimax over arm sets of size m and action sequences {y_t}

source.label: thm:lowerbd
source.quote: For any arm set $\AA$ and  action sequence $\{y_t\}_{t=1}^T\in\YY^T$, the minimax regret $R^\dagger_T$ satisfies $\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{R^\dagger_T }{(1-\epsilon_T)\sqrt{T\ln m/2}}=1$, where $\epsilon_T>0$  is  any parameter with $\lim_{T\to\infty}\epsilon_{T}=0$.

results.notes: Stated as an exact limit; proof only establishes the lower-bound direction. Recorded as asymptotic lower bound on minimax regret R^dagger_T.

source.label: thm:nearoptimaldivergingT
source.quote: If the parameter $\eta$ is chosen as $\eta_t=\sqrt{(8\ln m)/t}$ for $t\geq 1$, then for any arm set $\AA$ and action  sequence $\{y_t\}_{t=1}^T\in\YY^T$, the MARP procedure in Algorithm \ref{alg:MARP} satisfies, with probability at least $1-\delta$ for any $\delta\in(0,1)$, $R_T\leq \sqrt{2T\ln m} +\sqrt{\frac{\ln m}{8}} +  \sqrt{\frac{T}{2}\ln\frac{1}{\delta}}$

results.notes: gamma_t not stated in this theorem (presumably 1).
